chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Ibn Muskan, from some of his companions, who said:
Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: 'Among the happiness of a man is that he has children through whom he seeks assistance.'

key_terms.سَعَادَة: happiness/felicity (sa'ada) — a comprehensive term encompassing worldly well-being and spiritual blessing
key_terms.وُلْد: sons/children (wuld) — offspring, here indicating those who provide practical assistance
key_terms.يَسْتَعِينُ: seeks assistance (yasta'inu) — implying mutual benefit and reliance within the family unit

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Zayn al-Abidin say about the happiness of having children?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin, AS), the fourth Imam, identifies having helpful children as one of the markers of a man's felicity. This teaching reflects the traditional Islamic understanding of children not merely as a blessing but as a practical support in life's endeavors. The hadith appears in the opening chapter of Al-Kafi's Book of Marriage and Childbearing, contextualizing children within the framework of household welfare and family responsibility.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Ibn Muskan, from one of his companions who said,
‘Ali Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘From the happiness of the man is that there happens to be sons for him, (and he is) being assisted by them’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from ibn Muskan from certain persons of our people who has said the following: “
Ali ibn al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘It is of prosperity and good fortune of a man to have sons who help and support him.’”
